Chilean Steelmaker Invercap SA Exits Insolvency, Restarts Operations

SANTIAGO, June 13—Chilean steel producer Invercap SA has exited insolvency proceedings after creditors approved a restructuring plan, allowing the company to resume operations following months of uncertainty. The move is expected to stabilize supply chains in the country’s steel sector and secure hundreds of jobs that had been at risk.

Invercap SA, one of Chile’s leading steelmakers, entered court-supervised administration in January after struggling to manage mounting debts amid falling demand and rising input costs. The company’s facilities in the Biobío and Valparaíso regions operated at reduced capacity during the proceedings, affecting both local suppliers and downstream industries.

The restructuring plan, approved by over 80% of creditors last week, involves a combination of debt rescheduling and the sale of non-core assets. The company said it has secured new working capital to restore production and fulfill pending orders. “This agreement marks a new chapter for Invercap SA,” said CEO Rodrigo Martínez in a statement. “We are grateful for the support of our employees, partners, and creditors, and are fully committed to rebuilding trust in the market.”

Operations at the company’s main steel plant in Talcahuano resumed on Monday, with full production expected by the end of the month. The restart is set to bring back more than 700 workers who had been furloughed or shifted to part-time roles during the insolvency period.

Industry analysts welcomed the resolution, noting the potential positive impact on Chile’s construction and manufacturing sectors. “Invercap is a key supplier for a range of local industries, so its return to stability is good news for the entire value chain,” said María Eugenia Soto, an analyst at the Chilean Metals Association.

Union representatives expressed cautious optimism. “Our priority has always been job security for our members,” said union leader Felipe Araya. “We hope management will work closely with workers as the company returns to normal operations.”

Invercap SA’s exit from insolvency marks the end of a challenging period for the firm and offers relief to regional economies dependent on steel production.
